metaDescription: Instant guitar chord diagrams for any chord name — Cmaj7, Am7, D/F♯ and more. Open-position fingering for 100+ chords. Free web app and Chrome extension.
h2Decoder: How to decode a chord name
decoderIntro: Any chord symbol is built as: Root + quality + extensions + /optional bass. This table covers 95% of what you'll find in guitar tabs online.
rowRoot: C D E F G A B ± #/b
rowDom7: Major triad + minor 7th (♭7). The engine of blues and jazz.
rowHalfDim: Minor with lowered 5th + ♭7. Typical ii° chord.
rowSus: The 3rd is replaced by the 2nd or 4th (open sound, no major/minor color)
rowAdd: Adds the indicated note without a 7th.
rowSlash: Play the chord but put X in the bass.
callout: Diagram convention: you're looking at the neck face-on. The thinnest string (high E, 1st) is on the right; the thickest (low E, 6th) is on the left. Numbers above indicate the finger (1=index, 2=middle, 3=ring, 4=pinky). ○ = open string, ✕ = muted string.
extensionComingSoon: Coming soon on Chrome Web Store

pickingPageTitle: Dorian picking over the open low E string · Guitar Chords
pickingMetaDescription: Three Dorian-mode picking patterns using the open low E (6th) string as a pedal note. Ready-to-play fretboard diagrams.
pickingH1: Dorian picking over the open low E string
pickingLead: Three patterns for practicing the Dorian mode by weaving the open low E (6th) string in as a pedal note between the scale notes.
pickingIntro1: A pedal note is a fixed note repeated between the other notes of a phrase. Here the open low E (6th string) is the pedal while the Dorian melody moves on the strings above it: each scale note is picked, paired with the open E, building a cascading sound that's a staple of metal and prog rock playing.
pickingIntro2: Each diagram below shows the fretboard laid out horizontally, left to right, with all 6 strings from top (1st, high E) to bottom (6th, low E). The symbols on the left show whether a string is played open (○) or not used in that pattern (×). The black dots mark where to fret.
pickingFig1Alt: Fretboard diagram: pattern 1 of Dorian picking, B and G strings, with the open low E string
pickingFig2Alt: Fretboard diagram: pattern 2 of Dorian picking, high E and G strings, with the open low E string
pickingFig3Alt: Fretboard diagram: pattern 3 of Dorian picking, high E and B strings, with the open low E string
pickingFig3Caption: Pattern 3 — 1st (high E) and 2nd (B) strings, the sequence moves onto the treble strings.
pickingTip1: Start slow with a metronome and build up speed gradually; the priority is keeping the open E even every time it lands.
pickingTip2: Use alternate picking (down-up), or alternate pick and finger if you want the pedal note to ring out longer.
pickingTip3: Mute the unused strings with your palm or thumb so they don't ring along by accident.
